sub.en: Look at the verbs. Which ones take -ing after them, and which take to?

items.q: She decided ___ career at forty.
items.why: decide, want, hope, learn, choose → to + verb. enjoy, give up, finish, keep, don’t mind → verb + -ing.

acts.title: Three people who changed direction
text: ANNA, 44, was a bank manager for nineteen years. At forty she decided to learn the piano, which she had wanted to do since she was a teenager and had never had time for. Her first teacher told her, politely, that she was too old. She changed teacher. Four years later she still works at the bank, but she plays every evening and she does not mind practising the same eight bars for an hour. She says she is not going to become a pianist. She says it twice, which is once more than necessary.

JOÃO, 71, performed in concert halls for thirty years. Then an injury took the use of his left hand and he had to give up playing. He did not give up music: he learned to conduct instead, and he now stands in front of an orchestra four nights a month. “Everybody asks me if I miss it,” he says. “I miss it every day. I also enjoy this.”

MARAT, 29, passed his exams, left home, got a good job and got engaged, all in eighteen months. Then he stopped. He does not want to change career, he says — he wants to keep doing exactly what he does, and he wants everybody to stop asking him what is next.

acts.title: What people give up, and what they take up
text: A survey asked two thousand people over fifty what they had started and stopped in the last five years.
The most common thing to give up was not smoking or coffee. It was watching the news every morning. Almost a third had stopped, and most of them said they did not miss it.

The most common thing to take up was walking, followed by a language and then, surprisingly, a musical instrument. One in eleven had started learning an instrument after fifty, and of those, more than half had played as a child and given up as a teenager.
Only four per cent said they wanted to change career. Ninety per cent said they enjoyed having more time, and eighty per cent said they had no plan at all for the next five years and did not mind.

write.q: Write about three changes in your life: 6 sentences. One thing you decided to do, one you gave up, one you took up, one you don’t mind doing, and one you hope to do. Watch which verbs take -ing and which take to.
write.ph: Three years ago I decided to…
write.model: Three years ago I decided to change my job, and I have not regretted it once. I gave up working at the weekend, which was harder than leaving the company. I took up running in March, mostly so that I would stop looking at my phone in the morning. I don’t mind getting up at six for it. I hope to learn an instrument before I am forty — I’d always wanted to and I always found a reason not to. This year the reason has run out.

speak.q: Say four sentences out loud about your own changes: one with decided to, one with gave up, one with took up and one with hope to.
speak.model: I decided to change my job three years ago. I gave up working at the weekend. I took up running in March. I hope to learn the guitar before I’m forty.
